Shame on you Shane Gillis. You've shown us how you REALLY feel about women... and it's no joke: JANA HOCKING unleashes on the SNL comedian

If I had to guess Shane's motivation… could it be the average white guy who got rejected by women decided to turn the hurt and anger into a routine aimed at denigrating the opposite sex?

Actual Article Body:
By JANA HOCKING, COLUMNIST

Updated:  06:28 AEDT, 14 October 2026

It's always seemed to me Shane Gillis's stand-up acts simmer with rage. Listen and you can't unhear it – it's something close to hatred, if you will.

You may think this theory sounds ridiculous, considering he's technically a comedian, but having worked with quite a few stand-ups during my time as a radio and TV producer, one thing I quickly learned is that jokes are rarely just jokes. Behind every punchline is a hidden truth.

Whether it was the fat kid at school who figured out how to save face by making fun of themselves before anyone else could, or the kid who made his weirdness his entire schtick, the reason's baked in.

If I had to guess Shane's motivation… could it be the average white guy who got rejected by women decided to punch down and turn the hurt and anger into a routine aimed at denigrating the opposite sex?

During his Saturday Night Live monologue last week, Gillis made the mistake 'angry men' tend to make. He let the mask slip.

We heard the comedian's vile words on Saturday as he bombed spectacularly.

'I haven't been to the gym in so long, I didn't know women just dress like w***es now. Look, I'm sorry, there's no other way to describe [it]. Have you seen it? I've seen it. You've seen the shorts? They're those neon, like, artificial bait-colored [shorts], and the wrinkles go around the cheeks and all combine at the b******e. And don't look! You're not allowed to look.'

You could be forgiven for thinking someone had dug up an old SNL clip from 2006. But he said this in 2026, while we're still reeling from the allegations in the Cornell sexual assault case.

During his Saturday Night Live monologue last week, Shane Gillis made the mistake 'angry men' tend to make

Here's the thing about humor and hatred: They don't mix well

But go ahead, Shane… we'll wait for the punchline. Oh wait, there wasn't one, except a lame bit about being in the 'background of like 10 TikToks.'

He had the audacity to ask the audience whether they'd seen the shorts, but we know he was just encouraging knowing chuckles from the men in the room. Unfortunately for Shane, they would not be goaded.

Truth be told, I've seen how this plays out before. I was once in charge of producing a radio show with a comedian very similar to Shane. Oh, how he loved to crack misogynistic jokes.

There was the time he took aim at a female who had been publicly caught breaking lockdown during the Covid days. His hilarious one-liner on it was a nasty call to action: 'Go hang yourself.' As you can imagine, that landed us in a meeting with HR, which was then followed by an on-air apology.

Ironically, only days later, this thoroughly mediocre comedian would end up on the front page of the newspaper after he was caught breaking lockdown restrictions himself.

And I'll never forget the time he told his fellow female host during an ad break, 'If you interrupt me one more time while I'm talking, I will drag you out of this studio by the hair.' That hilarious 'banter' ended up with him being fired. If you ask me, he had it coming.

Because here's the thing about humor and hatred: They don't mix well.

Shane's routine on Saturday was damaging. I mean, even his sisters, who he called 'two big fat b***h sisters' weren't spared his cruelty. He described one as having 'trucker forearms,' – more obnoxious disparaging from the comedian who was fired from SNL in 2019 after podcast clips featuring anti-Asian slurs and derogatory remarks surfaced.

He recalled one sister calling him 'b***h hips' when he was a little kid laying on the floor watching television. By his own account, this insult has scarred him for life.

Now I'm no Freud, but you've got to wonder whether the women at the gym were getting the bill for the hurt his sisters caused him decades ago.

Could some of that childhood humiliation still be doing the talking? He'd just explained how deeply an insult from a woman could lodge, while handing out fresh ones to women who'd done nothing but get dressed for a workout.

Shane, buddy, are we discussing gym shorts, or are we still fighting over the TV remote?

It's, frankly, embarrassing. Not material for the stage but for his therapist's couch in my opinion.

Oh well, that's ok – probably only around five million people watched him make a fool of himself on live TV.

Wait, no, sorry, I just checked my notes. We should probably include the tens of millions of views Dan Levy's Instagram reel has garnered since he explicitly called out Shane's disgusting 'joke': 'Women wearing short shorts at the gym does not make them w***es. It makes the men calling them w***es misogynists.'

Hannah Einbinder, Viola Davis and Elizabeth Banks are among the celebrities who praised Dan's take-down.

Dan Levy's Instagram reel called out Shane's disgusting 'joke': 'Women wearing short shorts at the gym does not make them w***es. It makes the men calling them w***es misogynists'

Actress Elizabeth Banks commented in support on Dan Levy's Instagram reel: 'Nailed it'

Although he has been an SNL three times, Shane was fired as a cast member in 2019 after podcast clips featuring his anti-Asian slurs and derogatory remarks surfaced

Former 'SNL' Star Ego Nwodim took to Instagram on Monday to post an image of herself at the gym with the caption, 'W***e reporting for duty' – a better punchline than Gillis has ever delivered.

Smart, intelligent, funny women all absolutely miffed by Shane's mean-spirited, tone-deaf attempt at humor.

I mean, who can argue with Dan's clapback: 'I've seen more men's nipples at the gym than I've ever seen women showing their bodies off.'

A thoroughly reasonable observation, and one I'm happy to endorse.

I've seen men in gym tanks cut so generously down the sides that the shirt is essentially a necklace. Others eschew the top layer entirely.

Good for them. Enjoy the results, boys. Some of us women enjoy them too.

And yet, somehow, we manage to finish our workouts without deciding that the man on the chest press is asking for it because his shirt is skin-tight.

But a woman wears shorts that flatter her bottom and suddenly Shane labels her a w***e?

And describing those shorts as 'bait' invites another question: what, exactly, does he think the woman wearing them owes the man who looks? Or, worse, what does he think it gives him license to do?

Comedian Phoebe Robinson has urged Shane to write better material. I would offer a better solution: retire.

Oh, and get some therapy. Your hatred is not our problem and calling us w***es won't make it funny.

Shane Gillis Accused of Sexism After 'Saturday Night Live' Monologue: 'Women Just Dress Like Whores Now'

Comedian Shane Gillis is under fire after joking that "women just dress like whores" at gyms during his monologue on NBC's "Saturday Night Live."
The post Shane Gillis Accused of Sexism After ‘Saturday Night Live’ Monologue: ‘Women Just Dress Like Whores Now’ appeared first on Breitbart.

Actual Article Body:
Comedian Shane Gillis is under fire after joking that “women just dress like whores” at gyms during his monologue on NBC’s Saturday Night Live.

“I haven’t been in the gym in so long, I didn’t know women just dress like whores now,” Gillis joked during his recent SNL monologue.

“I’m sorry, there’s no other way to describe… have you seen it? I’ve seen it. The shorts. Have you seen the shorts?” the comedian continued, speaking directly to live audience members.

Gillis went on to make a joke about women dressing in revealing attire while exercising at gyms and then becoming offended if they catch men looking at their bodies, adding, “And don’t look. You’re not allowed to look.”

“For real, don’t look, because they are filming. I’m in the background of, like, ten TikToks right now,” the comedian further quipped.

Viewers took to social media to express their frustration with Gillis’ joke.

“My wife and I bought tickets for his Chicago show a while back and no joke we walked out in the first 15 minutes,” Reddit user wrote, before calling Gillis, “one of those ‘everything is allowed in comedy’ type morons,” adding, “He was racist, sexist, and homophobic.”

“I hate this fucking guy,” another declared. “He wants to be the pied piper of knuckle dragging shitheads so bad.”

“What the fuck am I, as a woman, meant to wear at the gym?” a third complained, adding, “Fucking stupid, ugly right-wing cunt.”

“The worst thing they can say about women is that we wear shorts,” another said. “How dare women wear SHORTS while EXERCISING.”

Actor Dan Levy also called out Gillis, describing the comedian as a “misogynist,” and even bizarrely going as far as to suggest the joke equates to “complacency” that leads to “sexual assault.”

“Women wearing short shorts to the gym does not make them whores,” Levy proclaimed puritanically, adding, “It makes the men calling them whores misogynists.”

Watch Below:

“I’m speechless that something like that can exist on live national television,” the Schitt’s Creek star continued. “And to be perfectly honest, more men need to be standing up in opposition to it.”

“Because it’s complacency that has created the environment in which women are sexually assaulted and it’s a ‘conversation’ as opposed to a ‘crime,'” Levy added.

The actor went on to demand that men “defend” women more, asserting, “This is not a women’s issue, this is an everybody issue.”

“The more that men objectify women in the media, the more that other men see them as objects and treat them as objects,” he added. “They are not objects, they are superior human beings to men.”

“And I’m sorry if this gets me in trouble with the internet, but fuck,” Levy concluded.
